model.name: Claim / Proposition
model.purpose: Provide a format-neutral record of a truth-apt assertion: what proposition is asserted, under what scope and qualification, by whom and with what standing, how it relates to other claims, which evidence and assessments it references, and how the claim record itself is identified, versioned, validated, restricted and disposed of. The model records assertion, not verdicts.
model.scope_statement: WM-KNW-007 covers the claim record as an object of knowledge management: propositional content and canonical form, identity and equivalence, scope and qualification (subject, place, time, conditions, measurand), stated calibrated uncertainty, the assertion act and asserting authority, provenance and ownership of the record, typed claim-to-claim relations, bound references to evidence and assessments, record lifecycle and versioning, well-formedness validation, sensitivity/access classification and disposition, and interoperability projections. It excludes the evidence items themselves, the appraisal of evidence bodies, the application and evaluation of inference schemes, the execution of fact-checking or verification, policy enforcement, and runtime audit trails owned by other systems.
in_scope: Canonical truth-apt statement, its language, atomicity and optional normalized subject-property-value or logical form
Claim identity, aliases, equivalence, restatement and translation relationships
Scope qualifiers: subject or population range, spatial extent, validity interval, conditions, assumptions, scenarios and known defeaters
Quantitative content of measurement claims: measurand, value, unit, stated coverage interval
Calibrated qualification stated on the claim: confidence and likelihood terms, scale reference and traceable-account pointer
The assertion act: claimant, role, illocutionary commitment, first and subsequent appearances, asserting authority and mandate
Provenance, attribution, derivation, ownership, stewardship and rights of the claim record
Typed claim-to-claim relations: entailment, specialization, contradiction, rebuttal, preference, supersession
Bound references to evidence items, external assessments/reviews and argument structures, carrying binding parameters only
Record lifecycle states, transitions, versioning, patch rules and externally issued retraction or correction references
Well-formedness shapes, required-field profiles and quality/testability signals for the record
Sensitivity classification, access policy expression, retention schedule, tombstones and disposition rules
Interoperability alignments and lossy-projection declarations across PROV-O, schema.org, VC 2.0, AIF, nanopublication and RDF 1.2
out_of_scope: Evidence items, citations, source descriptions, evidence typology, evidence appraisal and evidence lifecycle, which are owned by WM-KNW-008
Application and evaluation of inference, conflict and preference rules (AIF RA, CA and PA node semantics) and any defeasible-reasoning engine
Execution of fact-checking, verification or adjudication workflows, and the rating semantics, reviewer processes and audit trails of assessment systems
Runtime enforcement or evaluation of access and usage policies, and policy-decision logging
The real-world entities, events and quantities the claim is about, which belong to subject-domain models
Documents, publications and media that carry a claim, and publisher retraction workflows executed under NISO CREC
Cryptographic proof, credential status lists and verification procedures of Verifiable Credentials transport
Agent belief state, trust scoring of claimants or sources, and reputation computation
Storage engines, serializations and access interfaces (JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MCP, MongoDB are projections)
Generic knowledge-asset register mechanics inherited from the parent model WM-KNW-001

boundary_notes.distinction: This model carries the evidence reference, the binding role (supports, challenges, qualifies), directionality and a locally stated binding weight. It never carries the evidence item's description, provenance, appraisal grade or lifecycle; those are dereferenced from WM-KNW-008 and are never copied into a claim record.

A claim corresponds to the AIF I-node level. Applications of rules of inference (RA), conflict (CA) and preference (PA), argument-scheme definitions and any evaluation of argument acceptability belong to an argumentation model. This model records only that a claim occupies a premise or conclusion role in an externally identified argument structure.

This model holds the reviewable claim and a reference to reviews of it. The review's rating scale, reviewer identity workflow, publication and audit trail are owned by the reviewing system; a review reference is never read as a truth value on the claim record.

PROV terms are used as alignment for attribution, derivation, revision and invalidation of the claim record. This model does not own generic Activity/Agent modelling, provenance-of-provenance bundles or provenance query semantics.

A VC claim is a subject-property-value assertion carried inside a credential secured by proof. This model treats the proposition independently of transport: credential validity, status and cryptographic verification are owned by credential models and must not be interpreted as claim truth or claim lifecycle.

A quantitative claim references a measurand, a value with unit and a stated coverage interval. The measurement procedure, instrument, calibration and metrological traceability chain belong to a measurement or observation model.

This model expresses sensitivity classes and ODRL policies about claim records. ODRL is a policy expression language that defines no enforcement or evaluation semantics, and none is claimed here; decisioning and its logs belong to the adopting Dimension's platform.

Generic knowledge-asset identity, register governance, stewardship and licensing are inherited through the CHILD link. This model specializes only what makes a record truth-apt: proposition, qualification, assertion and claim relations.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Defines prov:Entity, prov:Activity, prov:Agent and the properties wasAttributedTo, wasDerivedFrom, wasQuotedFrom, wasRevisionOf, hadPrimarySource, generatedAtTime and invalidatedAtTime, plus the qualified-relation pattern and prov:Bundle. Grounds record provenance, attribution, derivation, revision and invalidation for claim records.

sources.title: Claim - Schema.org Type
sources.relevance: Defines Claim as a factually oriented claim that can be the itemReviewed of a ClaimReview, with text, name, about, sameAs, appearance, firstAppearance and claimInterpreter. Grounds canonical statement text, appearance context and the documented absence of formal claim-to-claim relations.

sources.title: ClaimReview - Schema.org Type
sources.relevance: Defines claimReviewed, itemReviewed, reviewRating, author and datePublished, and locates claimant and claim date on the reviewed item. Grounds the assessment-reference boundary: reviews are referenced, their ratings and workflow are not owned here.

sources.title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
sources.relevance: Defines a claim as 'an assertion made about a subject' in a subject-property-value structure, with credentialSubject, issuer, validFrom/validUntil, credentialStatus and proof. Grounds normalized claim form and the transport-versus-content boundary.

sources.title: The Argument Interchange Format (AIF) Specification
sources.organization: ARG-tech, Centre for Argument Technology, University of Dundee
sources.version_or_date: AIF specification document, published 2011 (AIF core ontology originating 2006)
sources.relevance: Defines the AIF upper ontology: I-nodes (information/propositions) and S-nodes covering applications of rules of inference (RA), conflict (CA) and preference (PA), with schematic form nodes. Grounds the claim = I-node mapping and the exclusion of inference, conflict and preference rule application.

sources.title: Nanopublication Guidelines (nschema)
sources.relevance: Specifies the head / assertion / provenance / publicationInfo named-graph pattern, the hasAssertion, hasProvenance and hasPublicationInfo predicates, and the instruction to limit assertion triples to the minimum so that credit attaches to a precisely defined statement. Grounds atomicity, the separation of assertion from record metadata, and projection guidance.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Requires date-time values with a seconds field and a time-offset of 'Z' or a numeric offset, and distinguishes '-00:00' (offset unknown) from 'Z'/'+00:00'. Grounds the model's timestamp rule and the separation of assertion time from ingestion time.

sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.relevance: Defines shapes graph, data graph, focus node, node and property shapes, constraint components, conformance and the severity levels sh:Violation, sh:Warning and sh:Info, and separates shapes from the processor that executes validation. Grounds the well-formedness finding and the validation-engine boundary.

sources.title: RDF 1.2 Concepts and Abstract Syntax
sources.relevance: Introduces triple terms and reifying triples (predicate rdf:reifies) that let a statement be named and described without being asserted, alongside named graphs and IRI-based identity. Grounds statement-level identity projection and the asserted-versus-unasserted distinction.

sources.title: Guidance Note for Lead Authors of the IPCC Fifth Assessment Report on Consistent Treatment of Uncertainties
sources.version_or_date: Mastrandrea et al., 2010; carried forward for AR6
sources.relevance: Defines the evidence (limited/medium/robust) and agreement (low/medium/high) axes, the five-level confidence scale, the likelihood scale with probability ranges, the requirement for traceable accounts, and the instruction to specify variables, region, time period and conditions in a finding. Grounds scope qualification and calibrated confidence.

sources.title: JCGM 200:2012 International vocabulary of metrology - Basic and general concepts and associated terms (VIM), 3rd edition
sources.organization: Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology (JCGM) / Bureau International des Poids et Mesures (BIPM)
sources.version_or_date: JCGM 200:2012, 3rd edition (2008 version with minor corrections)
sources.relevance: Provides the agreed terms measurand, measurement result, measurement uncertainty, coverage interval, coverage probability and metrological traceability. Grounds the quantitative-content finding and the boundary that measurement procedure and traceability chains belong to a metrology model.

sources.title: NISO RP-45-2024, Communication of Retractions, Removals, and Expressions of Concern (CREC)
sources.version_or_date: Recommended Practice, approved 26 June 2024, published 27 June 2024
sources.relevance: Defines best practice for creating, transferring and displaying retraction, removal and expression-of-concern metadata, with elements classified Essential, Essential if Available and Recommended, so that readers can identify an item's status. Grounds externally issued status-notice references and the rule that notice execution stays with publishers and aggregators.

sources.title: ODRL Information Model 2.2
sources.relevance: Defines Policy, Rule, Permission, Prohibition, Duty, Action, Asset, Party and Constraint as a policy expression language and states that it does not define enforcement or evaluation mechanisms. Grounds access-policy expression on claim records without granting enforcement semantics.

sources.title: FAIR Principles
sources.organization: GO FAIR International Support and Coordination Office
sources.version_or_date: Current published principles page, derived from the 2016 Scientific Data paper 'The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship'
sources.relevance: States F1 (globally unique and persistent identifiers), I3 (qualified references to other metadata) and R1.2 (detailed provenance). Grounds the identity priority, the requirement that claim relations and evidence bindings be qualified rather than bare links, and record provenance expectations.

bundles.name: Proposition Content and Identity
bundles.description: What proposition the record asserts, in what form, of what kind, and how that proposition is identified and recognised as the same claim across restatements, translations and systems.
bundles.rationale: Nothing else in the model is well defined until the asserted proposition is fixed as a single truth-apt statement with a stable identifier. Schema.org locates claim content in text/name/sameAs, VC 2.0 fixes a subject-property-value structure, the nanopublication guidelines require minimal precisely defined assertions, and RDF 1.2 supplies IRI and statement-level identity.

layers.name: Content and Form
layers.description: The canonical statement, its logical shape and its type, including the test that decides whether the content is truth-apt at all.

findings.name: Canonical Statement
findings.description: The single declarative sentence the record asserts, held in a canonical surface form with a language tag, an optional normalized structured form for machine comparison, and an atomicity rule of one record to one proposition.

questions.text: What single truth-apt proposition does this record assert, expressed as one declarative sentence?
Which normalized structured form represents the statement for machine comparison?
answer_data: Value, object or literal with datatype

questions.text: Does the statement bundle several separately assertable propositions that must be split into distinct records?
answer_data: Split or retain decision with rationale

questions.text: Is the canonical text a verbatim quotation of the claimant or a curator paraphrase, and in which language?
answer_data: Locator of the quoted passage if verbatim

data_elements.name: Canonical statement text
data_elements.description: The declarative sentence asserted by this record, stored exactly as curated.

data_elements.name: Statement language tag
data_elements.description: BCP 47 language tag of the canonical statement text.

data_elements.name: Normalized statement form
data_elements.description: Structured subject-property-value or logical rendering of the statement used for comparison and projection.

data_elements.name: Atomicity verdict
data_elements.description: Whether the statement passed the one-record-one-proposition test.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The canonical statement and its normalized form are the record's own primary field values, not a separately managed deliverable; the nanopublication guidance to keep assertions minimal implies inline triples rather than a document, and treating the statement as an artifact would create a second identity for the same proposition.

findings.name: Logical Form and Modality
findings.description: The structural properties that change what the statement asserts: polarity, quantification over the subject range, alethic or deontic modality, tense, and hedging that weakens the assertion.

questions.text: Is the assertion affirmative or negative, and does negation take wide or narrow scope?
answer_data: Contrast statement that the negation excludes

questions.text: Does the claim quantify universally, existentially or statistically over its subject range?
answer_data: Proportion or frequency expression if statistical

questions.text: What modality does the statement carry: factual, possible, necessary, obligatory or recommended?
Which hedges or qualifiers in the wording weaken the assertion, and are they preserved or moved into structured fields?

data_elements.name: Polarity
data_elements.description: Whether the proposition is asserted affirmatively or negatively.

data_elements.name: Quantification
data_elements.description: Quantifier over the subject range, with proportion where the claim is statistical.

data_elements.name: Modality
data_elements.description: Alethic or deontic modal force of the assertion.

data_elements.name: Hedge inventory
data_elements.description: Qualifying expressions detected in the statement that weaken its assertive force.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Polarity, quantification, modality and hedges are coded attributes of the statement itself. Externalizing them into an artifact would separate them from the sentence whose meaning they determine and would allow the two to drift apart under patching.

findings.name: Claim Type and Truth-Aptness
findings.description: The gate test that admits only truth-apt content to the register, and the classification of admitted claims by the kind of proposition asserted, which drives which scope and qualification fields are required.

questions.text: Is this content truth-apt, or is it a question, instruction, performative or bare preference that the register must reject?
answer_data: Rejection reason code where not truth-apt

questions.text: Which claim type applies: empirical, causal, comparative, predictive, definitional, classificatory, normative or evaluative?
answer_data: Secondary type where the claim is mixed

questions.text: Which scope, measurement and qualification fields does the assigned claim type make mandatory?
Under what conditions would this claim count as false, and is it falsifiable in principle?
answer_data: Note where the claim is definitional and not empirically falsifiable

data_elements.name: Truth-aptness verdict
data_elements.description: Whether the content can bear a truth value and may therefore be registered as a claim.

data_elements.name: Claim type code
data_elements.description: Concept from the governed claim-type scheme classifying the kind of proposition.

data_elements.name: Falsification condition
data_elements.description: Statement of what observation or argument would render the claim false.

artifacts.name: Claim Type Scheme
artifacts.description: Governed concept scheme of claim types with definitions, mutual-exclusion rules, and the per-type required-field profile that validation enforces.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Scheme IRI under the owning package namespace plus stable per-concept notations that survive label changes; releases carry a serial and digest, and retired concepts are marked deprecated with a successor rather than removed.

layers.name: Identity and Equivalence
layers.description: How a claim record is named, how aliases are held, and when two differently worded records are treated as the same proposition.

findings.name: Claim Identifier
findings.description: Assignment and resolution of the identifier that names this claim record, following the model's identity priority, with aliases for identifiers issued elsewhere and content digests kept only as secondary keys.

questions.text: Which authoritative master-system identifier, if any, already names this claim, and who issued it?
Which governed global identifier or IRI resolves to this claim record and stays resolvable for its retention period?
Which alternative identifiers name the same claim in other systems, and are they aliases or distinct records?
answer_data: Alias identifier list with issuing system

questions.text: Is any part of the identifier derived from a date, status or confidence value that would make it unstable?

data_elements.name: Primary claim identifier
data_elements.description: The single identifier of record for this claim, selected by the model's identity priority.

data_elements.name: Alias identifiers
data_elements.description: Identifiers naming the same claim in other systems, each with its issuing authority.

data_elements.name: Canonical content digest
data_elements.description: Digest over the canonical normalized statement, used only as a secondary equivalence key.

artifacts.name: Claim Identifier Register
artifacts.description: Register binding primary identifiers to claim records and to alias identifiers, recording the issuing authority, the identity-priority tier applied and the resolution commitment for each namespace.
artifacts.identity_strategy: The register itself is named by an IRI under the owning package namespace; entries are keyed by the primary claim identifier and are never reused for a different proposition, with retired entries retained as tombstones.

findings.name: Equivalence, Restatement and Translation
findings.description: The rules and recorded links that decide when a differently worded, summarised or translated statement is the same proposition, a restatement of it, or a genuinely different claim.

questions.text: Which other claim records state the same proposition in different words, and by what test was sameness established?
Is this record a translation of another claim, and which record is the authoritative language version?
Does a summarised or headline restatement drop scope qualifiers that the original claim carried?
Which superficially similar claim was deliberately kept separate, and why is it not the same proposition?

data_elements.name: Equivalence link
data_elements.description: Qualified link asserting that another claim record states the same proposition, with the test applied.

data_elements.name: Restatement link
data_elements.description: Qualified link to a paraphrase, summary or headline rendering of this claim, with direction and fidelity note.

data_elements.name: Translation link
data_elements.description: Link to another language version, naming the authoritative version.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Equivalence, restatement and translation are qualified reference edges between existing records. Materialising them as a separate artifact would duplicate identity state that the identifier register already holds and would risk the artifact and the edges disagreeing.

bundles.name: Scope, Qualification and Stated Uncertainty
bundles.description: The conditions under which the claim is asserted to hold: over what subjects, where, when, under what assumptions, with what measured content, and with what calibrated confidence the asserter attached to it.
bundles.rationale: The IPCC guidance requires a finding to specify its variables, region, time period and conditions, and to carry calibrated confidence and likelihood terms backed by a traceable account; JCGM 200 supplies the agreed terms for measurands and stated uncertainty. Without these, a claim is untestable and comparisons between claims are unsound.

layers.name: Scope Qualifiers
layers.description: Subject range, spatial and temporal extent, and the conditions, assumptions and known defeaters that bound the assertion.

findings.name: Subject and Population Scope
findings.description: The entities the claim ranges over: the named subject or the population definition with inclusion and exclusion criteria, and the level of aggregation at which the claim is asserted.

questions.text: Which entity or population is the claim about, identified rather than merely named in prose?
answer_data: Subject reference to a domain identifier
Fallback description where no identifier exists

questions.text: Which inclusion and exclusion criteria delimit the population, and what is explicitly outside it?
At which level of aggregation does the claim hold: individual, group, cohort or population average?
answer_data: Warning where the claim may be read as an individual-level assertion

questions.text: Does the claim name an identifiable natural person, and does that trigger sensitivity classification?

data_elements.name: Subject reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the entity or class the claim is about, resolved against a subject-domain model.

data_elements.name: Population definition
data_elements.description: Inclusion and exclusion criteria delimiting the range of the claim.

data_elements.name: Aggregation level
data_elements.description: The level at which the claim is asserted to hold.

data_elements.name: Identifiable person flag
data_elements.description: Whether the statement names or renders identifiable a natural person.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Subject and population scope are per-claim field values and references to subject-domain identifiers. Publishing them as an artifact would either duplicate the domain model's entity descriptions or create a parallel population registry this model has no mandate to own.

findings.name: Spatial and Temporal Scope
findings.description: Where and for what period the claim is asserted to hold, kept strictly separate from when it was asserted and when the record was captured.

questions.text: For which geographic or jurisdictional extent is the claim asserted to hold?
Over which validity interval does the claim assert its content to be true?
answer_data: Validity end instant or open-ended marker
Reference period or baseline where comparative

questions.text: How does the validity interval differ from the assertion time and from the record ingestion time?
Is the claim asserted as timeless, as time-indexed, or as a forecast about a future interval?

data_elements.name: Spatial extent reference
data_elements.description: Place, region or jurisdiction over which the claim is asserted to hold.

data_elements.name: Validity interval
data_elements.description: Start and end of the period for which the claim's content is asserted true, in RFC 3339 with seconds and offset.

data_elements.name: Assertion timestamp
data_elements.description: When the claim was asserted by the claimant, distinct from record capture.

data_elements.name: Record ingestion timestamp
data_elements.description: When this register captured or observed the claim.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are timestamp and reference fields on the record. Their governance value comes from being adjacent to the statement they qualify; an artifact would add an indirection that makes the crucial event-time versus ingestion-time distinction easier to lose in projection.

findings.name: Conditions, Assumptions and Known Defeaters
findings.description: The scenario, background assumptions, ceteris paribus conditions and explicitly acknowledged defeating circumstances under which the claim is or is not asserted to hold.

questions.text: Under which scenario, model or set of background assumptions is the claim asserted?
Which circumstances, if they obtained, would defeat the claim without falsifying it outright?
Which conditions are load-bearing such that changing them creates a different claim rather than a variant?
Are any assumptions implicit in the wording and not yet stated in structured fields?

data_elements.name: Scenario reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the scenario, pathway or model under which the claim is asserted.

data_elements.name: Assumption statement
data_elements.description: A background condition the claim depends on, stated explicitly.

data_elements.name: Known defeater
data_elements.description: An acknowledged circumstance that would defeat the claim, with its defeater type.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Conditions and defeaters qualify one specific claim and are meaningless detached from it. Recording a defeater is a note that a defeating circumstance is acknowledged; evaluating whether it actually defeats the claim belongs to an argumentation model, so no local artifact should imply that adjudication happened here.

layers.name: Quantified Content and Calibrated Uncertainty
layers.description: Measured content of quantitative claims and the calibrated confidence or likelihood term the asserter attached, with the traceable account that justifies it held elsewhere.

findings.name: Quantitative Content and Measurand
findings.description: For claims asserting a quantity: the measurand as defined, the value and unit, the stated uncertainty as a coverage interval with its coverage probability, and the comparison basis where the claim is comparative.

questions.text: What exactly is the measurand, defined precisely enough that two parties would measure the same thing?
answer_data: Conditions that must hold for the definition to apply

questions.text: What value and unit does the claim assert, and in which unit system?
answer_data: Unit system and any conversion applied

questions.text: What stated uncertainty accompanies the value, and at what coverage probability?
answer_data: Whether the interval is stated by the claimant or derived by the curator

questions.text: Against which baseline, reference value or comparator is a comparative quantitative claim asserted?
answer_data: Reference period or population for the comparator

data_elements.name: Measurand definition
data_elements.description: The quantity intended to be measured, defined per metrological practice.

data_elements.name: Asserted quantity value
data_elements.description: Numeric value with unit asserted by the claim.

data_elements.name: Stated coverage interval
data_elements.description: Interval attributed to the measurand with its coverage probability, as stated in the claim.

data_elements.name: Comparator reference
data_elements.description: Baseline or comparator against which a comparative quantitative claim is asserted.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Value, unit and stated interval are per-claim fields. The measurement procedure, calibration and metrological traceability chain that would justify an artifact belong to a metrology or observation model, so producing one here would assert ownership of measurement semantics this model explicitly disclaims.

findings.name: Calibrated Confidence and Likelihood
findings.description: The calibrated qualification the asserter attached to the claim, expressed with a registered scale term, plus the pointer to the traceable account that justifies it. The appraisal of the underlying evidence body is not held here.

questions.text: Which registered scale and term express the confidence attached to this claim, and who set it?
Where the claim is probabilistic, which likelihood term or probability range is asserted?
answer_data: Whether the range is asserted or interpreted from prose

questions.text: Which traceable account documents the reasoning behind the stated confidence, and where does it live?
Is any evidence-body appraisal grade being carried here that should instead be dereferenced from the evidence model?

data_elements.name: Confidence term
data_elements.description: Calibrated confidence term drawn from the registered scale in force.

data_elements.name: Likelihood term or range
data_elements.description: Calibrated likelihood term with its probability range where the claim is probabilistic.

data_elements.name: Traceable account reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the documented reasoning that justifies the stated confidence.

data_elements.name: Confidence scale binding
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the calibrated scale under which the terms are interpreted.

artifacts.name: Calibrated Uncertainty Scale Registry
artifacts.description: Registry of the confidence and likelihood scales the owning package permits, each with its ordered terms, the probability ranges bound to likelihood terms, and the rule that terms are never compared across scale versions without explicit mapping.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Registry IRI under the owning package namespace with per-scale identifiers and per-term notations; each release carries a serial and digest, and records cite scale identifier plus version so that a later scale revision never silently reinterprets an existing claim.

bundles.name: Assertion, Provenance and Ownership
bundles.description: Who asserted the claim and with what standing, how the claim record came to exist, and who is accountable for it.
bundles.rationale: PROV-O supplies attribution, derivation, primary-source and revision terms; the nanopublication pattern separates assertion metadata from record metadata; VC 2.0 fixes the issuer as the party asserting claims; FAIR R1.2 requires detailed provenance. Together these ground both the assertion act and the record's own lineage and stewardship.

layers.name: Assertion Acts and Standing
layers.description: The act of asserting: claimant, commitment, appearance context, and whether the claimant held authority to assert.

findings.name: Claimant and Assertion Act
findings.description: Who asserted the proposition, in what capacity and with what degree of commitment, together with the first and subsequent contexts in which the assertion appeared.

questions.text: Which agent asserted this proposition, identified rather than described by name alone?
In what capacity did the claimant assert it: personally, on behalf of an organisation, or as a reported position?
answer_data: Reporting chain where the assertion is second-hand

questions.text: How strong was the commitment: asserted outright, hypothesised, attributed to others, or quoted without endorsement?
answer_data: Wording that signals the commitment level

questions.text: Where did the claim first appear and where else has it appeared since?
answer_data: Medium and audience for each appearance

data_elements.name: Claimant reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the agent that asserted the proposition.

data_elements.name: Assertion capacity
data_elements.description: The capacity in which the claimant asserted, including representation of an organisation.

data_elements.name: Commitment level
data_elements.description: Degree of assertive commitment, from outright assertion to unendorsed quotation.

data_elements.name: Appearance locator
data_elements.description: Locator of an occurrence of the claim, with its timestamp, marking which is the first appearance.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The assertion act is captured as references to agents and to appearance locations in documents owned by content and publication models. Creating an artifact here would duplicate those documents and would blur the line between recording that an assertion occurred and republishing the material that carried it.

findings.name: Asserting Authority and Mandate
findings.description: Whether the claimant held a recognised mandate to assert within a jurisdiction or domain, and the standing that mandate gives the claim, recorded without treating standing as truth.

questions.text: Under which mandate, remit or delegated authority did the claimant assert this proposition?
Within which jurisdiction or domain is that authority recognised, and where is it not?
Is the claim official, advisory or unofficial in standing, and what follows from that classification?
answer_data: Consequences declared by the owning package

questions.text: What prevents authority standing from being read as a truth verdict on the claim?

data_elements.name: Mandate reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the mandate or remit under which the claimant asserted.

data_elements.name: Recognised jurisdiction
data_elements.description: Jurisdictions or domains in which the asserting authority is recognised.

data_elements.name: Standing classification
data_elements.description: Official, advisory or unofficial standing of the assertion.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Mandates are instruments issued and maintained by the granting bodies; this model holds a reference and a standing classification only. Producing a local artifact would imply this register certifies authority, which it does not, and would create a competing copy of an external legal or institutional instrument.

layers.name: Record Provenance, Ownership and Rights
layers.description: How the claim record itself was produced and derived, who owns and stewards it, and under what rights it may be reused.

findings.name: Record Derivation and Attribution
findings.description: The lineage of the claim record: which source it was derived or quoted from, which primary source stands behind it, which agent or process extracted it, and which revision it succeeds.

questions.text: From which prior entity was this claim record derived, quoted or revised?
answer_data: Primary source reference where the chain is known

questions.text: Which agent or automated process generated the record, and was extraction human, assisted or fully automated?
answer_data: Model or tool identifier and version where automated

questions.text: Which activity produced the record, and when did it start and complete?
answer_data: Start and end timestamps in RFC 3339 with offset
Relationship to the separately recorded assertion time

questions.text: What confidence attaches to the extraction itself, as distinct from the claim's own stated confidence?
answer_data: Known extraction failure modes for this source type

data_elements.name: Derivation reference
data_elements.description: Qualified link to the entity this record was derived from, quoted from or revised from.

data_elements.name: Generating agent
data_elements.description: Agent or automated process responsible for generating the record.

data_elements.name: Extraction method
data_elements.description: How the claim was captured: manual curation, assisted extraction or automated extraction, with tool version.

data_elements.name: Extraction confidence
data_elements.description: Confidence in the fidelity of extraction, kept distinct from the claim's stated confidence.

artifacts.name: Claim Record Provenance Bundle
artifacts.description: A named provenance description set for one or more claim records, holding derivation, attribution, generation activity and revision statements in a form that can itself be attributed and dated, following the PROV bundle and nanopublication provenance-graph pattern.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bundle IRI under the owning package namespace, bound to the primary claim identifiers it describes; each bundle carries its own attribution and generation timestamp so that provenance of the provenance is expressible, and bundles are appended rather than edited.

findings.name: Ownership, Stewardship and Rights
findings.description: Which package owns the claim record, who stewards it, which roles may change it, and under what licence or rights the statement and the record may be reused.

questions.text: Which package owns this claim record and which named steward is accountable for it?
Which roles may change the statement, the scope qualifiers, the status and the sensitivity class?
Under which licence or rights statement may the claim record and its canonical text be reused?
What happens to ownership when the owning package is retired or transferred?

data_elements.name: Owning package reference
data_elements.description: The package accountable for the claim record.

data_elements.name: Accountable steward
data_elements.description: Named individual or role accountable for the record's content and status.

data_elements.name: Rights statement
data_elements.description: Licence or rights terms governing reuse of the record and its canonical text.

artifacts.name: Stewardship and Rights Declaration
artifacts.description: Declaration naming the owning package, the accountable steward, the role-to-field write matrix, the licence applying to records and to quoted statement text, and the succession rule if ownership is transferred.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Declaration IRI under the owning package namespace with a serial per release and a digest; each claim record cites the serial in force at its last status transition so that historical governance terms remain reconstructable.

bundles.name: Claim Relations and External Bindings
bundles.description: How claims stand to one another and how a claim binds to evidence, assessments and argument structures owned elsewhere.
bundles.rationale: AIF supplies the typology of inference, conflict and preference relations at the argument level and locates propositions as I-nodes; PROV supplies revision and invalidation; FAIR I3 requires qualified rather than bare references; schema.org documents that it defines no claim-to-claim relations, which makes this a real modelling need. Bindings must carry parameters only, since evidence, review and argument content are owned by other models.

layers.name: Typed Claim-to-Claim Relations
layers.description: Recorded relations between claim records: entailment and specialization, conflict, and preference or supersession, registered without being adjudicated.

findings.name: Entailment and Specialization
findings.description: Relations where one claim's content stands to another as implication, generalization, specialization or presupposition, recorded as qualified edges with the ground on which the relation is asserted.

questions.text: Which other claims does this claim entail, and on what ground is entailment asserted?
Which broader claim does this one specialize, and which narrower claims specialize it?
What does this claim presuppose that must hold for it to be evaluable at all?
Which relation assertions are curator judgements rather than derived from a formal rule?

data_elements.name: Entailment edge
data_elements.description: Qualified edge asserting that this claim entails a target claim, with its ground.

data_elements.name: Specialization edge
data_elements.description: Qualified edge to a broader or narrower claim, naming the dimension of specialization.

data_elements.name: Presupposition edge
data_elements.description: Qualified edge to a claim that must hold for this claim to be evaluable.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are typed edges between records in the same register, matching the model's declared TYPED-EDGES link type. Externalising them would duplicate graph state and would tempt consumers to read a curated edge list as a derived inference result, which this model does not produce.

findings.name: Conflict and Contradiction
findings.description: Registration that two claims stand in conflict, with the conflict type and the point of disagreement recorded, and with resolution explicitly not performed here.

questions.text: Which claims contradict this one, and is the conflict rebutting the content or undercutting its support?
Is the apparent conflict genuine, or does it dissolve once scope qualifiers are compared?
Who registered the conflict and when, and what status does registration confer on either claim?
answer_data: Status effect declared by the owning package

questions.text: Which system, outside this model, is responsible for resolving or adjudicating the conflict?
answer_data: Expected form of the resolution output

data_elements.name: Conflict edge
data_elements.description: Qualified edge registering conflict with another claim, with conflict type and disagreement point.

data_elements.name: Conflict registration event
data_elements.description: Who registered the conflict and when, in RFC 3339 with offset.

data_elements.name: Resolution referral
data_elements.description: Reference to the external body or system responsible for adjudicating the conflict.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Conflicts are registered as qualified edges plus a registration event. A conflict register artifact would read as an adjudication docket and would encroach on the argumentation model that owns conflict-rule application and on the assessment systems that issue verdicts.

findings.name: Preference and Supersession
findings.description: Recorded orderings between claims: an asserted preference between competing claims, and the supersession chain by which a later claim replaces an earlier one.

questions.text: Which competing claim is preferred over which, and by whose criterion?
answer_data: Asserting agent and date of the preference

questions.text: Which claim does this one supersede, and which claim supersedes it?
Does supersession change the earlier claim's status, or leave it valid for its original period?
How are supersession chains kept acyclic and traversable to the current claim?

data_elements.name: Preference edge
data_elements.description: Qualified edge asserting preference between two competing claims, with criterion and asserter.

data_elements.name: Supersedes reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the claim this record supersedes.

data_elements.name: Superseded-by reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the claim that supersedes this record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Preference and supersession are directional edges evaluated at query time to find the current claim. Materialising a chain artifact would freeze a view that must stay derivable from the edges, and preference application in argument evaluation is owned by the argumentation model.

layers.name: External Bindings
layers.description: Qualified references from a claim to evidence items, external assessments and argument structures, carrying binding parameters only.

findings.name: Evidence Link Binding
findings.description: The qualified reference from this claim to an evidence item in WM-KNW-008, carrying the target identifier, the binding role, directionality and a locally stated binding weight, and nothing describing the evidence itself.

questions.text: Which evidence items are bound to this claim, identified by resolvable WM-KNW-008 identifiers?
In what role does each bound item stand: supporting, challenging, qualifying or merely cited?
answer_data: Curator note on the role assignment

questions.text: What weight or relevance does this claim's curator attach to the binding, and how is that distinguished from the evidence's own appraisal?
answer_data: Explicit statement that evidence appraisal grades are not stored here

questions.text: What happens to the binding when the referenced evidence record is revised, withdrawn or deleted by its owner?
answer_data: Local status effect on the claim

data_elements.name: Evidence reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of an evidence item in WM-KNW-008 bound to this claim.

data_elements.name: Binding role
data_elements.description: Role the referenced item plays relative to this claim: supports, challenges, qualifies or cites.

data_elements.name: Locally stated binding weight
data_elements.description: Curator-stated relevance or strength of this specific binding, explicitly not an evidence appraisal grade.

data_elements.name: Binding status
data_elements.description: Whether the binding is active, dangling or retired following changes at the target.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The binding is a qualified edge with a small parameter set, and by the REFERENCE contract with WM-KNW-008 nothing describing the evidence may be held locally. Any artifact here would inevitably accrete evidence metadata and would duplicate the target model's records.

findings.name: Assessment and Review Reference
findings.description: References from this claim to externally issued assessments, fact-checks or reviews of it, recorded so that consumers can find them without this model owning ratings, reviewer workflow or review audit trails.

questions.text: Which external reviews or assessments name this claim as the item reviewed?
Which rating scale did each review use, and is that scale interpretable outside its issuing system?
answer_data: Prohibition on normalising ratings across issuers

questions.text: What effect, if any, does a review reference have on this claim record's own status?
answer_data: Cases where a review triggers a dispute status

questions.text: Who owns the review's workflow, evidence and audit trail, and what may this model never copy from it?

data_elements.name: Assessment reference
data_elements.description: Identifier or locator of an external review or assessment of this claim.

data_elements.name: Reviewing organisation
data_elements.description: Organisation or person that issued the referenced assessment.

data_elements.name: Rating scale reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the issuing system's rating scale, held as an opaque reference and not normalised locally.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Reviews are documents produced and governed by fact-checking and assessment systems. This model stores only resolvable references, because producing a local artifact would amount to republishing verdicts and would assert ownership of rating semantics and reviewer audit trails that belong to those systems.

findings.name: Argument Structure Role Reference
findings.description: The record that this claim occupies a premise or conclusion role in an externally identified argument structure, mapped to the AIF I-node level, without any local representation of inference-scheme application.

questions.text: In which externally identified argument structures does this claim appear, and in what role?
How does the claim map to the AIF I-node level, and which node types are deliberately not represented here?
answer_data: Excluded node types (RA, CA, PA, F)

questions.text: What prevents an argument role reference from being read as an evaluated inference or an accepted conclusion?
Which registered model will own argument-scheme definition and evaluation once it exists?

data_elements.name: Argument structure reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of an external argument structure in which this claim participates.

data_elements.name: Argument role
data_elements.description: Role the claim plays in the referenced structure.

data_elements.name: Node-type mapping note
data_elements.description: Statement of the AIF node level this record maps to and the node types excluded from local representation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Only a role reference is held, because AIF rule-application nodes and scheme definitions belong to an argumentation model that is not yet registered. Producing an argument artifact here would create exactly the ownership overlap the boundary review is meant to prevent.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, Validation and Record Governance
bundles.description: The states a claim record passes through, how it is versioned and corrected, how its well-formedness and quality are checked, and how it is restricted, retained and disposed of.
bundles.rationale: PROV supplies revision and invalidation semantics, NISO CREC supplies the metadata practice for externally issued retractions and expressions of concern, SHACL supplies shapes and severity-graded conformance separated from the processor, and ODRL supplies policy expression that explicitly excludes enforcement. These fix a governance surface for the record without claiming execution.

layers.name: Record Lifecycle and Change Control
layers.description: States and transitions of the claim record, the rule separating a new version from a new claim, and references to externally issued status notices.

findings.name: Status and State Transitions
findings.description: The permitted states of a claim record, the transitions between them, who may perform each transition, and the terminal timestamps and successor references that transitions set.

questions.text: Which status does the record currently hold, and since which instant?
answer_data: Status effective timestamp in RFC 3339 with offset

questions.text: Which transitions are permitted from the current status, and which roles may perform them?
Which preconditions must be satisfied before a record may leave draft and be treated as asserted?
What does a terminal status set on the record, and what must remain readable afterwards?
answer_data: Fields that must remain readable after termination

data_elements.name: Record status
data_elements.description: Current lifecycle state of the claim record.

data_elements.name: Status effective timestamp
data_elements.description: Instant from which the current status applies, in RFC 3339 with seconds and offset.

data_elements.name: Invalidation timestamp
data_elements.description: Instant at which the record ceased to be current, where a terminal status applies.

data_elements.name: Transition record
data_elements.description: Actor, reason, prior status and timestamp for each status change of this record.

artifacts.name: Claim Lifecycle State Scheme
artifacts.description: Definition of the permitted record states, the legal transitions between them, the role authorised for each transition, the preconditions for promotion out of draft, and the fields each terminal state must set.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Scheme IRI under the owning package namespace with stable per-state notations; releases are serialised with a digest, and records cite the scheme version under which their last transition was made so historical transitions stay interpretable.

findings.name: Versioning and Change Control
findings.description: The rule distinguishing a version patch from a new claim, the immutability of asserted statement text, and the version manifest that lets any prior state of the record be reconstructed.

questions.text: Which changes are version patches to this record and which create a new claim linked by supersession?
Which fields are immutable once the record is asserted, and how are typographic corrections handled?
How is a specific prior version of the record cited and retrieved?
Which precondition must a patch declare so that concurrent edits cannot silently overwrite each other?

data_elements.name: Version identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a specific version of the claim record.

data_elements.name: Prior version reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the version this one revises.

data_elements.name: Change classification
data_elements.description: Whether a change was a patch or triggered creation of a new claim.

artifacts.name: Claim Version Manifest
artifacts.description: Manifest listing each version of a claim record with its version identifier, digest, prior-version reference, change classification and effective timestamp, sufficient to reconstruct any prior state of the record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Manifest keyed by the primary claim identifier, with monotonically increasing version identifiers that contain no date component; each entry is append-only and carries a digest over the canonical serialization of that version.

findings.name: Retraction, Correction and Status Notices
findings.description: References to notices issued outside this model — retractions, removals, corrections and expressions of concern — and the local status effect they trigger, with issuance and propagation remaining with the issuing publisher or authority.

questions.text: Which externally issued notice affects this claim, of what type, and who issued it?
answer_data: Notice type (retraction, removal, correction, expression of concern)

questions.text: Which local status change does the notice trigger, and is the change automatic or reviewed?
How must a claim affected by a notice be displayed to downstream consumers?
Who is responsible for issuing, publishing and propagating the notice itself, as opposed to referencing it here?
answer_data: Escalation route where a notice is missing or wrong

data_elements.name: Status notice reference
data_elements.description: Locator of an externally issued retraction, removal, correction or expression-of-concern notice affecting the claim.

data_elements.name: Notice type
data_elements.description: Type of the referenced notice as classified by its issuer.

data_elements.name: Notice issuance timestamp
data_elements.description: When the issuer published the notice, in RFC 3339 with seconds and offset.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Retraction and correction notices are artifacts created, published and propagated by publishers, aggregators and issuing authorities under their own recommended practice. This model records a reference and the local status effect only; producing a notice artifact here would claim issuance authority and would duplicate a document whose canonical version lives with its issuer.

layers.name: Validation and Quality
layers.description: Structural well-formedness of the claim record and the quality signals that indicate whether it is specific and testable enough to be useful.

findings.name: Well-Formedness, Quality and Testability
findings.description: The shapes and required-field profiles the record must satisfy, the severity grading of failures, and the quality signals — specificity, ambiguity, unresolved scope, testability — that gate promotion. Shapes are owned here; execution is not.

questions.text: Which shapes and required-field profile apply to this record given its claim type?
Which constraint failures are violations that block promotion and which are warnings that only annotate?
Which quality signals indicate that the statement is too vague, ambiguous or under-scoped to be testable?
Which component executes validation, and what does this model own as against that executor?
answer_data: Handling of processor-reported failures as distinct from violations

data_elements.name: Applicable shapes reference
data_elements.description: Serial and digest of the shapes package under which the record was last validated.

data_elements.name: Conformance result
data_elements.description: Whether the record conformed, with severity-graded results attached.

data_elements.name: Quality signal set
data_elements.description: Specificity, ambiguity, unresolved-scope and testability signals computed for the record.

data_elements.name: Promotion blocker
data_elements.description: An outstanding violation preventing the record from leaving draft.

artifacts.name: Claim Shapes Package

bundles.name: Interoperability and Agent Operation
bundles.description: How claim records project onto external vocabularies without claiming conformance, and how an agent bootstraps into the model and exchanges records safely.
bundles.rationale: Multiple standards model overlapping but non-identical notions of a claim: schema.org as a creative work, VC 2.0 as a subject-property-value assertion inside a credential, AIF as an I-node, nanopublications as an assertion graph, and RDF 1.2 as a triple term that may be named without being asserted. Recording these as alignments with declared losses, and providing an explicit bootstrap contract, is what makes the model operable by an agent.
