data_elements.name: Decision-local evidential weight
data_elements.description: Weight assigned to the cited evidence for this decision, on a named local scale.

data_elements.name: Referenced certainty grade
data_elements.description: Certainty or quality grade read from WM-KNW-008 and carried unchanged, with the framework and read time that qualify it.

data_elements.name: Sufficiency judgement
data_elements.description: Whether the cited evidence was judged sufficient, insufficient or indeterminate for the reason it supports.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The appraisal is a decision-local qualifier on an existing citation binding, not a document. Emitting it as an artefact would produce something that reads like an evidence assessment report and would compete with the grading that WM-KNW-008 owns, blurring exactly the distinction this finding exists to preserve between the evidence, its intrinsic grade and one decision's judgement of its bearing. Keeping it inline forces every reader to encounter the appraisal attached to the specific reason it qualifies.

findings.name: Assumptions, dependencies and defeat conditions
findings.description: Statements the reasoning rests on that are recorded as assumed rather than supported, the external conditions, inputs and third-party commitments the reasoning depends on, the conditions under which an assumption would be considered defeated, the period or context for which it is asserted to hold, and the party recorded as responsible for its continued validity. This model records assumptions; it does not monitor, test in production or enforce them.

questions.text: Which statements are recorded as assumptions rather than as supported premises, and how is that marking made explicit?
answer_data: explicit assumption marker distinguishing it from a supported premise
reference to the argument element the assumption qualifies

questions.text: On what external condition, input, dataset or third-party commitment does the recorded reasoning depend?
answer_data: reference to the depended-on condition, input or commitment
note on whether the dependency was verified at decision time

questions.text: Under what stated condition would an assumption be considered defeated?
answer_data: reference to the observable or input whose change triggers it
consequence the record states would follow for the affected argument

questions.text: For what stated period or context is the assumption asserted to hold?
answer_data: validity window expressed with explicit start and end where bounded
context qualifier limiting where the assumption applies
marker for assumptions asserted without any stated bound

questions.text: Who is recorded as responsible for an assumption's continued validity, given that this model performs no monitoring?
answer_data: reference to the monitoring or review arrangement held outside this model
explicit statement that no monitoring function is exposed here

data_elements.name: Assumption statement
data_elements.description: A statement the reasoning rests on that is recorded as assumed rather than supported.

data_elements.name: Dependency reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an external condition, input or third-party commitment the recorded reasoning depends on.

data_elements.name: Defeat condition
data_elements.description: Condition whose occurrence the record states would defeat the assumption and the argument resting on it.

data_elements.name: Assumption validity window
data_elements.description: Period or context for which the assumption is asserted to hold, with explicit bounds where stated.

data_elements.name: Assumption responsibility reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party recorded as responsible for the assumption's continued validity; monitoring is executed elsewhere.

artifacts.name: Assumption and dependency register
artifacts.description: The consolidated register of assumptions, dependencies, defeat conditions and validity windows for one decision, generated from the canonical assumption records so that a third party can see what the reasoning rests on.
media_or_form: rendered annex to the decision record
artifacts.identity_strategy: Register identity derives from the decision's master-system identifier plus the register key; individual rows use a governed identifier where one exists and otherwise a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension.

findings.name: Uncertainty and confidence qualifiers
findings.description: Confidence qualifiers attached to reasons, inferences and the rationale as a whole: the scale used, whether the qualifier is about the evidence, the inference or the outcome holding in practice, the stated limits of knowledge beyond which the reasoning should not be relied on, and how a verbal qualifier maps to any numeric range. The model records the qualifier as asserted and does not compute or validate calibration.

questions.text: What confidence qualifier is attached to the rationale as a whole, and on which named and published scale is it expressed?
answer_data: scale identifier with its published level definitions
the element the qualifier is attached to

questions.text: Is the qualifier a statement about the evidence, about the inference, or about the outcome holding in practice?
answer_data: note where a single qualifier was asserted over several subjects at once

questions.text: What are the stated limits of knowledge beyond which the recorded reasoning should not be relied on?
answer_data: conditions or populations explicitly excluded from the reasoning
reference to the assumption records that bound the reasoning

questions.text: How is a calibrated verbal qualifier mapped to a numeric range, and is that mapping published with the record?
answer_data: publication location of the scale definition
flag where a verbal qualifier is used with no published mapping

data_elements.name: Confidence qualifier
data_elements.description: Asserted confidence value attached to a reason, inference or the rationale as a whole.

data_elements.name: Confidence scale reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the named scale whose published level definitions give the qualifier meaning.

data_elements.name: Confidence subject
data_elements.description: Whether the qualifier speaks to the evidence, the inference or the outcome holding in practice.

data_elements.name: Knowledge limit statement
data_elements.description: Stated conditions beyond which the recorded reasoning is declared not to apply.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Confidence is a qualifier on something else — a reason, an inference, an appraisal or the whole rationale — and has no standing apart from what it qualifies. Extracting qualifiers into their own artefact would detach a confidence level from the statement it modifies, which is the specific failure mode calibrated-language guidance exists to prevent, and would let a summary confidence figure circulate without its scale definition or knowledge limits. Qualifiers are therefore inline and always travel with their subject and scale reference.

layers.name: Robustness and contestation
layers.description: Recorded trade-offs and sensitivity of the reasoning to its inputs, and the counterarguments, counter-evidence, objections, dispositions and dissenting or minority positions recorded against it.

findings.name: Trade-offs and sensitivity of the reasoning
findings.description: What was traded against what, which disbenefits are recorded as accepted, which inputs or assumptions would change the recorded outcome and within what range, any switching value at which the preferred option would change, and whether the varied inputs are disclosed well enough for a qualified third party to reproduce the finding. This model records the results and the disclosure; it does not run the analysis.

questions.text: Which benefits and disbenefits were traded against each other, and which disbenefits are recorded as knowingly accepted?
answer_data: references to the criteria in the `core` split that each side maps to

questions.text: Which inputs or assumptions, if changed, are recorded as changing the outcome, and over what stated range were they varied?
answer_data: range or set of values over which each was varied
recorded effect on the outcome for each variation

questions.text: What switching value or threshold is recorded at which the preferred option would change?
answer_data: switching value with units and the variable it applies to
the option that would become preferred beyond it
note where no switching value could be identified

questions.text: Are the varied inputs and method disclosed well enough for a qualified third party to see how the result was reached?
answer_data: disclosure statement covering inputs, method and data sources
reference to the analysis record or dataset held outside this model
gap marker where disclosure is incomplete

questions.text: Does the record state that no sensitivity analysis was performed, and what reason is given?
answer_data: reference to any waiver or proportionality argument relied on

data_elements.name: Trade-off statement
data_elements.description: Statement of what was traded against what in reaching the recorded outcome.

data_elements.name: Accepted disbenefit
data_elements.description: A disbenefit the record states was knowingly accepted as part of the trade-off.

data_elements.name: Sensitivity variable reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an input or assumption whose variation was tested, with the range over which it was varied.

data_elements.name: Switching value
data_elements.description: Value of a variable at which the recorded preference between options would change.

data_elements.name: Reproducibility disclosure note
data_elements.description: Statement of inputs, method and sources sufficient for a qualified third party to follow how the result was reached.

artifacts.name: Sensitivity and trade-off record
artifacts.description: The presented record of trade-offs, varied inputs, ranges, outcomes and any switching value for one analysis run supporting the decision.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the decision's master-system identifier plus the artefact-kind key and a zero-padded run sequence; the analysis it reports is referenced by its own identifier and is not owned here.

findings.name: Counterarguments, objections and dissent
findings.description: Counter-arguments and counter-evidence recorded against a reason or inference, who raised them, how each was dispositioned in the rationale, which argument elements are marked defeated by a recorded challenge, and any minority or dissenting position preserved as an attributed statement rather than folded into the majority rationale. Adjudication authority, approval workflow and role assignment stay with the `governance` split.

questions.text: What counter-argument or counter-evidence is recorded, and which reason or inference does it attack?
answer_data: reference to the attacked reason, premise or inference
reference to any counter-evidence citation binding

questions.text: Who raised the objection and in what stated capacity, without this model assigning their role?
answer_data: capacity as stated in the record

questions.text: How was the objection dispositioned in the rationale: accepted, rebutted, undercut or left open?
answer_data: disposition statement with its stated ground
time and asserting party of the disposition

questions.text: Is a minority or dissenting position preserved as an attributed position rather than merged into the majority rationale?
answer_data: attribution reference for the dissenting party
explicit marker separating it from the majority rationale

questions.text: Which argument elements are marked as defeated by a recorded challenge, and what does that marking not change?
answer_data: defeated marking on the affected argument element
reference to the challenge that produced it
explicit note that the marking annotates the argument and does not alter the recorded outcome or decision state

data_elements.name: Objection statement
data_elements.description: Counter-argument, objection or counter-evidence recorded against a reason or inference, captured as stated.

data_elements.name: Objection target reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the reason, premise or inference the objection attacks.

data_elements.name: Objection disposition
data_elements.description: How the objection was dealt with in the rationale: accepted, rebutted, undercut or left open.

data_elements.name: Dissent attribution reference
data_elements.description: Reference identifying the party whose minority or dissenting position is recorded.

data_elements.name: Defeated marking
data_elements.description: Annotation marking an argument element as defeated by a recorded challenge; an argument-level marking only.

artifacts.name: Dissenting or minority opinion
artifacts.description: An attributed statement of a minority or dissenting position preserved alongside the majority rationale, together with the objections it rests on.
media_or_form: rendered annex to the decision notice
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the decision's master-system identifier plus the artefact-kind key and a zero-padded sequence per dissenting party; attribution references the party record held outside this model.

bundles.name: Explanation and reasoning provenance
bundles.description: Explainable decision traces and bounded, audience-scoped explanation renditions produced from the recorded rationale, together with the provenance of the reasoning itself and the separation of authored rationale from machine-generated explanation.
bundles.rationale: Explainability guidance requires an explanation to be meaningful to its recipient and accurate to the process that generated the output, and EU law gives affected persons a right to clear and meaningful explanations of an AI system's role in a decision. A provenance vocabulary supplies the attribution terms, including software agents, needed to say who or what produced the reasoning. This bundle separates the rendition given to an audience from the reasoning it renders and from the provenance of that reasoning.

layers.name: Decision traces, renditions and reasoning provenance
layers.description: The ordered trace from inputs to recorded outcome, the bounded renditions produced for declared audiences with their faithfulness and omission statements, and the provenance of the reasoning including authorship mode and generating agent.

findings.name: Explainable decision trace and bounded explanation renditions
findings.description: The ordered sequence of reasoning steps recorded as the trace from inputs to the recorded outcome, and the audience-scoped explanations produced from it. Each rendition declares its audience, what was omitted or replaced by a reference, the rationale revision it renders, and an assertion that it reflects the recorded reasoning rather than a post-hoc narrative. A rendition is an explanation, not an audit record: audit trails and access logging are owned by the `governance` split.

questions.text: What ordered sequence of reasoning steps is recorded as the trace from inputs to the recorded outcome?
answer_data: ordered trace step entries with explicit sequence keys
reference from each step to the reason, inference or binding it corresponds to
inputs entering the trace, carried as references

questions.text: For which audience is a rendition produced, and what does the record state was omitted or replaced by a reference for that audience?
answer_data: audience code and the entitlement or duty the rendition answers
omission set listing what was withheld and on what stated ground
reference to the omission policy held by the `governance` split

questions.text: How is a rendition asserted to reflect the recorded reasoning rather than a plausible reconstruction of it?
answer_data: faithfulness assertion with the method used to derive the rendition
identifier and revision of the rationale record set rendered
marker where the rendition is a summary rather than a complete restatement

questions.text: What are the declared bounds of the trace: which steps are recorded in full, which are summarised, and which are not captured at all?
answer_data: trace completeness declaration per step class
list of step classes explicitly not captured
reference to the system boundary beyond which steps are not observable

questions.text: How is each issued rendition identified and linked back to the rationale revision it renders?
answer_data: rendition identifier with its serial sequence
rationale record set identifier and revision
content digest of the rendition as issued

data_elements.name: Trace step
data_elements.description: One recorded reasoning step in the ordered trace, referencing the reason, inference or binding it corresponds to.

data_elements.name: Explanation audience
data_elements.description: Declared audience a rendition is produced for, and the entitlement or duty it answers.

data_elements.name: Faithfulness assertion
data_elements.description: Assertion that the rendition reflects the recorded reasoning, naming the derivation method and the rationale revision rendered.

data_elements.name: Explanation omission note
data_elements.description: Record of what was omitted or replaced by a reference in a rendition and on what stated ground.

artifacts.name: Explanation rendition
artifacts.description: An audience-scoped explanation issued from the recorded rationale, carrying its audience, omission set, faithfulness assertion and the rationale revision it renders.
media_or_form: rendered notice supplied to a recipient
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the decision's master-system identifier plus the artefact-kind key and a zero-padded issuance sequence; each issuance additionally carries a content digest and the rendered rationale revision.

artifacts.name: Reasoning trace record
artifacts.description: The ordered trace of reasoning steps from inputs to recorded outcome, with its completeness declaration; a description of reasoning, not an audit log.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Derived from the decision's master-system identifier plus the trace key; steps use explicit sequence numbers and never derive identity from their timestamps.

findings.name: Reasoning provenance and authored versus generated rationale
findings.description: Who or what produced the recorded reasoning: whether it was authored by a person, generated by a software agent, or generated then edited; which agent, model version and configuration produced any machine-generated text; what prior rationale, template or precedent it was derived from; and the separation of the time the reasoning was asserted from the time the record was observed or ingested. Machine-generated explanation must be labelled so that it is never read as an authored reason.

questions.text: Was the rationale authored by a person, generated by a software agent, or generated and then edited by a person?
answer_data: reference to the responsible human agent where one exists
reference to the generating activity where machine generation occurred

questions.text: Which software agent, model version and configuration produced a machine-generated explanation?
answer_data: model or tool version string and configuration reference
association between the agent and the generating activity

questions.text: At what time was the reasoning asserted, and at what time was the record of it observed or ingested?
answer_data: asserted time with explicit seconds and offset
recorded or ingested time with explicit seconds and offset
note where the two are equal because the record is the original assertion

questions.text: From which prior rationale, template or precedent was this reasoning derived?
answer_data: reference to the source rationale, template or precedent
note on what was changed relative to the source

questions.text: How is machine-generated explanation labelled so that a reader cannot mistake it for a reason asserted by the decision authority?
answer_data: generated-content label applied at every projection
reference to the human agent who reviewed or adopted the generated text, where any did
rule statement covering how the label survives export and rendering

data_elements.name: Rationale authorship mode
data_elements.description: Whether the rationale was authored, machine-generated, or generated and then edited by a person.

data_elements.name: Generating agent reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the software agent, with model version and configuration, that produced machine-generated explanation.

data_elements.name: Reasoning asserted time
data_elements.description: Time the reasoning was asserted by its author or generating agent, as an event time.

data_elements.name: Record observation time
data_elements.description: Time the rationale record was observed or ingested by the rationale store, recorded separately from the asserted time.

data_elements.name: Derived-from reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a prior rationale, template or precedent from which this reasoning was derived.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Reasoning provenance qualifies every other record in this model rather than standing on its own: authorship mode, generating agent and the two timestamps must travel with the reason, appraisal, objection or rendition they describe, or the labelling requirement for machine-generated content fails exactly where it matters. A separate provenance artefact would also duplicate the agent and activity records that the provenance vocabulary places outside this model, and would let a rendition circulate stripped of its generated-content label. Provenance is therefore carried inline on each record and projected into artefacts as attribution metadata.

bundles.name: Decision authority, mandate and participation
bundles.description: Establishes who was competent to take the decision, under which mandate and delegation, who is accountable for the resulting record, who participated in which declared role, and what integrity conditions applied to that participation.
bundles.rationale: A decision is only authoritative if the deciding body acted within a mandate and the participation conditions prescribed for it. ISO 15489-1 makes assigned responsibilities and mandate-driven records requirements a precondition of authoritative evidence; PROV qualifies responsibility, association and delegation; the Council's Rules of Procedure show mandate, quorum and proxy representation as explicit, recorded facts.

layers.name: Mandate, deciding authority and accountable roles
layers.description: The competence chain: the authority that decided, the instrument that empowered it, the delegations exercised beneath it, and the standing roles accountable for the decision record afterwards.

findings.name: Deciding authority and mandate binding
findings.description: Identifies the body, office or role that took the decision and binds it to the mandate instrument, its subject and jurisdictional limits, its validity window and its succession path. Records the authority as an attributable agent rather than as free text.

questions.text: Which authoritative master-system identifier designates the body or office that took this decision, and under which mandate instrument did it act?
answer_data: Deciding authority reference resolved against the party or governing-body register
Mandate instrument reference with its issuing authority
Statement of which system of record issued the authority identifier

questions.text: What subject-matter, monetary or jurisdictional limits does the mandate place on this authority, and what is the recorded consequence of acting outside them?
answer_data: Enumerated mandate scope limits with units where quantified
Ultra vires handling code and the status the decision takes if a limit is breached
Reference to the reviewing forum competent to determine the breach

questions.text: Over which validity window was the mandate in force at the instant the decision was taken?
answer_data: Mandate validity start and end as RFC 3339 timestamps with explicit offset
Decision event time compared against that window
Flag indicating whether the comparison was asserted or externally verified

questions.text: Which alternate or successor authority becomes responsible if the deciding body is dissolved, merged or renamed?
answer_data: Successor authority reference with the transfer instrument reference
Retained historical authority reference for the original decision

data_elements.name: Deciding authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the body, office or role that took the decision, resolved against the authoritative party or governing-body register.

data_elements.name: Mandate instrument reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the statute, charter, terms of reference, delegation instrument or standing order that confers competence for this decision.

data_elements.name: Mandate scope limit
data_elements.description: A declared limit on the mandate expressed as subject-matter, monetary ceiling, geography or term.

data_elements.name: Mandate validity window
data_elements.description: Start and end instants during which the mandate was in force, each an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Authority succession reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the successor or alternate authority and to the instrument effecting the succession.

artifacts.name: Decision authority and delegation register
artifacts.description: A governed register of deciding authorities, their mandate instruments, scope limits, validity windows and the delegations issued beneath them, against which any individual decision's authority claim is resolved. It is a register of competence, not a record of decisions taken.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identity is taken from the authoritative master-system identifier of the governing-body or decision-rights register maintained by the adopting Dimension; failing that, a governed IRI assigned by a recognised registry; failing both, a ULID minted by the adopting Dimension and flagged as Dimension-assigned. Register entries are keyed by authority identifier plus mandate instrument identifier, never by adoption date or meeting name.

findings.name: Delegation, sub-delegation and proxy representation
findings.description: Records the chain from the mandate holder to the person or system that actually exercised the decision, with the ceiling and validity window on each step, whether sub-delegation was permitted, and how a vote or act exercised on behalf of another participant is captured.

questions.text: Which delegation or sub-delegation steps link the mandate holder to the agent that actually exercised this decision?
answer_data: Ordered delegation chain entries, each naming delegator, delegate and instrument
Qualified delegation reference aligned to the PROV delegation pattern
Indicator of whether each step was standing or ad hoc

questions.text: What ceiling applies to each delegation step, and is further sub-delegation permitted at that step?
answer_data: Ceiling value and unit per step
Sub-delegation permitted flag with the authorising clause reference
Escalation target when the ceiling is exceeded

questions.text: How is a delegation revoked or withdrawn, and what is the effect on decisions already taken under it?
answer_data: Revocation instrument reference and effective instant
Retrospectivity code stating whether prior decisions remain valid
Ratification requirement flag for acts taken after revocation

questions.text: When an act or vote was exercised on behalf of another participant, how is that representation recorded?
answer_data: Proxy entry naming represented party, representing party and the authorising provision
Limit on the number of parties one participant may represent
Whether the proxy counted towards the participation threshold

data_elements.name: Delegation chain entry
data_elements.description: One step of delegated competence, naming delegator, delegate, instrument reference and ordinal position in the chain.

data_elements.name: Delegation ceiling
data_elements.description: The quantified limit attached to a delegation step, with value, unit and basis.

data_elements.name: Delegation validity window
data_elements.description: Start and end instants of a delegation step as RFC 3339 timestamps with explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Delegation revocation reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the instrument revoking or withdrawing a delegation, with its retrospectivity code.

data_elements.name: Proxy representation entry
data_elements.description: Record that one participant acted on behalf of another, naming both parties and the authorising provision.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Delegation facts are short reference structures resolved against dr-gov-art-authority-register and mirrored into the lifecycle ledger; they carry no independent document body. The delegation instrument itself is a document owned and published by the issuing authority, so materialising a second artefact here would duplicate an external record and create a competing copy of a mandate this model does not own.

findings.name: Owner, steward, custodian and reviewer assignment
findings.description: Assigns the standing accountabilities over the decision record after it is taken: who owns it, who maintains its governance metadata, who holds physical or logical custody of its projections, and who is obliged to review it. Distinguishes accountability for governance metadata from accountability for the substance of the decision.

questions.text: Who is the accountable owner of this decision record, and how does that accountability differ from those of the steward, custodian and reviewer?
answer_data: Party references for owner, steward, custodian and reviewer
Responsibility statement per role drawn from the adopting Dimension's role catalogue
Indicator of whether a role is held by a person, an office or an organisational unit

questions.text: Which role is answerable for the accuracy of the governance metadata as distinct from the correctness of the decision itself?
answer_data: Named role accountable for governance metadata accuracy
Named authority accountable for decision substance
Escalation path when the two disagree

questions.text: How is a role assignment transferred when the holder leaves, and from which instant does the successor's accountability run?
answer_data: Handover event reference with predecessor and successor party references
Handover effective instant as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z
Whether the predecessor retains residual accountability for the prior period

questions.text: Which role holds the authority to release this decision to a wider audience or to publish it?
answer_data: Constraint stating whether release requires the deciding authority's concurrence
Reference to the access schedule entry that the release must satisfy

data_elements.name: Governance owner reference
data_elements.description: Party or office accountable for the decision record as a governed asset.

data_elements.name: Steward reference
data_elements.description: Party accountable for the accuracy and completeness of the decision's governance metadata.

data_elements.name: Custodian reference

data_elements.name: Reviewer reference

data_elements.name: Role handover entry
data_elements.description: Transfer of a named role from predecessor to successor with its effective instant and residual-accountability flag.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Role assignments are reference tuples pointing at party identifiers held in an external identity model; they have no document body of their own and change independently of the decision content. Materialising them as an artefact would create a stale local copy of party master data and a second, competing source of truth for accountability that the adopting Dimension's role catalogue already owns.

layers.name: Participation, decision rule and integrity of participation
layers.description: Who took part in which declared capacity, under which decision rule and participation threshold, and what was declared, determined and acted upon regarding conflicts of interest.

findings.name: Participant roster, declared roles and applicable decision rule
findings.description: Captures the participants and their declared roles, the entitlement to vote or object, the decision rule that governed the taking of the decision, the mode of proceeding, and the attestation that any required participation threshold was met.

questions.text: Which participants took part, in which declared roles, and which of them were entitled to vote or formally object?
answer_data: Participant entries with party reference and declared role code
Alignment of role codes to a controlled role vocabulary such as a top-level role classification

questions.text: Which decision rule applied — unanimity, qualified or simple majority, consensus, silence or written procedure — and where is that rule prescribed?
answer_data: Decision rule code from a controlled vocabulary
Reference to the rules of procedure clause prescribing it
Threshold expression where the rule is numeric

questions.text: Was the participation threshold or quorum asserted as satisfied, by whom, and on what stated basis?
answer_data: Quorum attestation with attesting party reference and attestation instant
Counted and required participation figures as asserted
Explicit statement that this is the presiding authority's assertion, not an evaluation performed by this model

questions.text: How is a decision taken by written or silence procedure distinguished from one taken in a convened sitting?
answer_data: Participation mode code covering convened, written, silence and delegated modes
Objection window for silence procedure with its closing instant
Reference to the minutes or proceedings record where one exists

questions.text: How is an abstention or formal objection referenced without reproducing the dissent record owned by the reasoning area?
answer_data: Abstention or objection event entry with participant reference and instant
Pointer to dr-rsn-art-dissent-record by identifier only
Rule stating that dissent content, arguments and grounds are not stored here

data_elements.name: Participant entry
data_elements.description: One participant with party reference, declared role code, voting entitlement flag and attendance or response state.

data_elements.name: Decision rule code
data_elements.description: Controlled code naming the rule under which the decision was taken, with a reference to the prescribing provision.

data_elements.name: Quorum attestation
data_elements.description: Assertion by a named presiding party that the participation threshold was satisfied, with counted and required figures and the attestation instant.

data_elements.name: Participation mode code
data_elements.description: Code distinguishing convened sitting, written procedure, silence procedure and delegated exercise.

data_elements.name: Dissent record reference
data_elements.description: Identifier-only pointer to the dissent artefact owned by the reasoning area; no dissent content is stored locally.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The participation surface is a roster of references plus a small set of coded assertions; the narrative proceedings that would justify a document already exist as minutes or a proceedings record owned by the convening body and, where reasoning is involved, as the reasoning area's artefacts. Holding these facts inline keeps them queryable and avoids creating a rival account of the sitting that this model has no authority to issue.

findings.name: Declared interests, conflict determination and recusal
findings.description: Records interests declared by participants before or during the decision, who determined whether a declared interest was disqualifying, the recusal or mitigation action taken, and the effect of recusal on the applicable participation threshold.

questions.text: Which interests were declared by participants in relation to this decision, and against which register entry was each declaration recorded?
answer_data: Interest declaration entries with declaring party, interest type and declaration instant
Reference to the interests register entry where one is maintained
Indicator of whether the declaration was standing or decision-specific

questions.text: Who determined that a declared interest was disqualifying, and what recusal or mitigation action followed?
answer_data: Determining party reference and determination instant
Determination outcome code and stated grounds reference
Recusal or mitigation action code such as withdrawal, non-participation in the vote, or supervised participation

questions.text: How does a recusal change the participation threshold or decision rule applied to the affected item?
answer_data: Statement of whether the recused participant counted towards presence
Reference to the provision governing the adjustment

questions.text: For how long must interest declarations and conflict determinations remain retrievable after the decision is closed, and under what lawful basis?
answer_data: Retention period reference for declarations, separate from the decision's own period
Lawful basis reference where the declarations contain personal data
Masking or minimisation requirement applicable at disclosure

data_elements.name: Interest declaration entry
data_elements.description: A declared interest with declaring party reference, interest type code, declaration instant and optional register entry reference.

data_elements.name: Conflict determination
data_elements.description: The determination on a declared interest, naming the determining party, outcome code, grounds reference and determination instant.

data_elements.name: Recusal action code
data_elements.description: Coded action taken in consequence of a disqualifying interest, such as withdrawal, abstention from the vote or supervised participation.

data_elements.name: Recusal effective time
data_elements.description: Instant from which the recusal took effect, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Declaration personal-data flag
data_elements.description: Indicator that a declaration contains personal data and is therefore subject to minimisation and to a lawful-basis-bound retention period.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Declarations and determinations are short, strongly typed assertions that must remain individually queryable for threshold recomputation and disclosure masking, and they frequently contain personal data whose minimisation is easier to enforce at field level than in a document body. Where a jurisdiction requires a standing register of interests, that register is an external instrument owned by the integrity authority and is referenced rather than reissued here.

bundles.name: Approval, status lifecycle and change control
bundles.description: How the decision moved from submission through review to approval or ratification, which validity state it holds and why, how it may be reviewed, appealed, reconsidered or reopened, and how its versions, changes and content provenance are controlled.
bundles.rationale: Authoritative decision records require an explicit, transition-controlled state model with recorded effective dating, a supersession and consolidation chain, and attributable change history. RFC 2026 demonstrates staged maturity, retirement to a historic state and a bounded appeals procedure; the ELI ontology supplies in-force, consolidation and repeal relations; Akoma Ntoso supplies FRBR-level version identity and lifecycle events; PROV-O supplies attribution, revision and invalidation.

layers.name: Submission, approval, status and reconsideration
layers.description: The approval pipeline binding, the controlled status and validity model with its effective dating and conditions, and the triggers and windows for review, appeal, reconsideration and reopening.

findings.name: Submission, review and approval stage binding
findings.description: Records which governance stages the decision passed, which are mandatory before it can take effect, and the identifier of the external approval or ratification activity that evidences each stage. Distinguishes approval from ratification and from non-binding endorsement.

questions.text: Which submission, review, approval and ratification stages did this decision pass, and which of them are mandatory before it can take effect?
answer_data: Ordered stage entries with stage code, outcome code and completion instant
Reference to the procedure that prescribes the stage sequence

questions.text: Which external approval activity record evidences each stage, and which identifier binds the two?
answer_data: Approval activity reference per stage resolved against WM-ACT-024
Binding identifier and the resolution method for it
Statement that activity execution and completion semantics are not held locally

questions.text: What distinguishes approval from ratification and from non-binding endorsement in this governance context?
answer_data: Definitions of approval, ratification and endorsement as used by the adopting Dimension
Legal or procedural effect of each on the decision's validity
Which of them can retrospectively cure an act taken beyond delegated authority

questions.text: What happens to the decision when a mandatory stage is skipped, completed out of order, or completed by an unauthorised party?
answer_data: Defect code and the status assigned to a defectively approved decision
Remediation path such as ratification, re-submission or withdrawal

data_elements.name: Approval stage entry
data_elements.description: One governance stage with stage code, mandatory flag, outcome code, deciding party reference and completion instant.

data_elements.name: Approval activity reference
data_elements.description: Identifier-only reference to the external approval or ratification activity record that evidences a stage.

data_elements.name: Approval defect code
data_elements.description: Coded defect in the approval pipeline, such as a skipped mandatory stage or an unauthorised approver.

data_elements.name: Ratification reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a ratifying act that cures a defect or confirms an act taken under delegated or urgent procedure.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Stages are carried as thin bindings to approval activity records that live in WM-ACT-024; the substantive approval evidence, including approver identity, execution and completion, is that model's artefact. Creating a governance document for the pipeline here would reproduce an approval record this model does not own and would introduce a second, divergent statement of whether approval occurred.

findings.name: Status, validity and conditional effectiveness
findings.description: Holds the controlled status of the decision and its permitted transitions, the separation of approval, publication and effective instants, the conditions attached to a conditional decision and who confirms them, and identifier-only references to follow-up implementation or monitoring obligations.

questions.text: Which status does this decision hold now, and which controlled vocabulary defines the permitted values and the legal transitions between them?
answer_data: Current status code from the governed status vocabulary covering draft, submitted, approved, effective, conditional, suspended, superseded, revoked, expired and reopened
Transition table naming permitted source and target states
Authority competent to perform each transition

questions.text: From which instant is the decision effective, and how does that differ from the instants at which it was approved and published?
answer_data: Effective instant, approval instant and publication instant as separate RFC 3339 timestamps with explicit offsets or Z
Indicator of retrospective effect where the effective instant precedes approval
Ingestion instant recorded separately from all three

questions.text: Which conditions precedent or subsequent must hold for a conditional decision to become or remain effective, and who confirms their satisfaction?
answer_data: Condition entries with condition text reference, type and due instant
Confirming party reference and confirmation instant
Consequence code applied when a condition fails

questions.text: Which follow-up implementation or monitoring obligations are attached by reference, and which model owns their execution?
answer_data: Follow-up obligation references with obligation type and owning model identifier
Reporting-back instant or interval where one is stipulated
Explicit statement that implementation progress and outcome measurement are not stored here

questions.text: What causes automatic expiry as opposed to explicit revocation or suspension, and how is each distinguished in the record?
answer_data: Expiry rule reference and the computed or stipulated expiry instant
Revocation and suspension entries with acting authority, ground code and effective instant
Rule preventing an expired decision from being silently treated as revoked

data_elements.name: Status code
data_elements.description: Current governed status of the decision drawn from the controlled status vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Status transition entry
data_elements.description: A recorded transition with source status, target status, acting authority reference, ground code and effective instant.

data_elements.name: Effective time
data_elements.description: Instant from which the decision has effect, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z, held separately from approval and publication instants.

data_elements.name: Effectiveness condition entry
data_elements.description: A condition precedent or subsequent with type, due instant, confirming party reference and satisfaction state.

data_elements.name: Follow-up obligation reference
data_elements.description: Identifier-only reference to an implementation or monitoring obligation arising from the decision, together with the model that owns its execution.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Status, effective dating and conditions are the queryable control fields that determine whether the decision may be relied upon at a given instant, so they must be first-class inline data rather than text inside a document. Follow-up obligations are deliberately reference-only because implementation progress, monitoring results and outcome measurement are executed and evidenced by other models; issuing an artefact here would invite those execution facts to accumulate locally.

findings.name: Review, appeal, reconsideration and reopening
findings.description: Defines what triggers a scheduled or event-driven review, who may appeal or seek reconsideration to which forum within what time limit, on what grounds a closed decision may be reopened and what status it then takes, and how a review outcome is linked to the original decision without overwriting it.

questions.text: What triggers a scheduled or event-driven review of this decision, and by which due instant must the review occur?
answer_data: Review trigger code covering fixed interval, condition breach, external change and complaint
Review due instant as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z
Party obliged to initiate the review

questions.text: Who may appeal or request reconsideration, to which forum, and within what time limit from which starting instant?
answer_data: Eligible appellant classes and the forum reference for each escalation tier
Time limit expressed as a duration with the instant from which it runs
Whether the forum's determination is final on procedure, on merits, or on both

questions.text: On what grounds may a closed decision be reopened, and which status does it hold while reopened?
answer_data: Reopening ground codes such as new evidence, procedural defect or material change of circumstance
Status held during reopening and whether the original remains effective meanwhile
Authority competent to authorise the reopening

questions.text: How is the outcome of a review, appeal or reconsideration linked to the original decision without overwriting it?
answer_data: Outcome reference with relation type such as confirms, varies, remits or quashes
Reference to an external legal judgment where the forum is judicial
Rule that the original version remains retrievable in its approved form

data_elements.name: Review trigger code
data_elements.description: Coded reason a review becomes due, whether periodic, conditional or event-driven.

data_elements.name: Review due time
data_elements.description: Instant by which a due review must be conducted, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Appeal window
data_elements.description: Duration within which an appeal or reconsideration request must be lodged, with the instant from which it runs.

data_elements.name: Appeal forum reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the forum competent to hear an appeal at a given escalation tier.

data_elements.name: Review outcome reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the reviewing or appellate determination, with the relation it bears to the original decision.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Triggers, windows, forums and outcome links are scheduling and relationship data that must drive obligations and queries rather than be read out of a document. The substantive review or appellate determination is itself a decision or a legal judgment owned by another record, so this finding deliberately holds only the pointer and the relation type and creates no artefact that could be mistaken for the determination.

layers.name: Version history and provenance of decision content
layers.description: The authoritative version chain with supersession and consolidation, the append-only ledger of governance changes with attributable agents and separated time axes, and the provenance of the governed decision content itself.

findings.name: Version identity and append-only change ledger
findings.description: Establishes which version is authoritative, which prior versions it supersedes or consolidates, and an append-only ledger of governance changes recording the acting agent, the reason, the authority relied on, the significance of the change and the separated event, observation and ingestion instants.

questions.text: Which version of this decision is authoritative now, and which prior versions does it supersede, consolidate or repeal?
answer_data: Version identifier distinct from the decision master identifier
Supersedes, consolidates and repeals references to prior versions
Statement of which version applies to a stated instant

questions.text: For each ledger entry, which agent made the change, for what stated reason, and under which authority?
answer_data: Acting agent reference with qualified role
Change reason code and free-reference to the authorising instrument
Whether the agent acted on delegated authority and under which delegation entry

questions.text: How are event time, observation time and ingestion time recorded separately for a single ledger entry?
answer_data: Event instant of the governance act itself
Observation or attestation instant when the fact was witnessed or reported
Ingestion instant when the Vercy record captured it, each an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z

questions.text: Which changes are editorial and which are substantive enough to require re-approval or a new version?
answer_data: Change significance code distinguishing editorial, corrective and substantive
Re-approval requirement flag driven by the significance code
Erratum reference where an approved version is corrected rather than replaced

data_elements.name: Version identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a specific governed version of the decision, distinct from and subordinate to the decision master identifier.

data_elements.name: Supersession reference
data_elements.description: Reference from the current version to the version or decision it supersedes, consolidates or repeals, with the relation type.

data_elements.name: Lifecycle ledger entry
data_elements.description: An append-only entry recording one governance act with acting agent, reason code, authority reference, significance code and its separated time axes.

data_elements.name: Event time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the recorded governance act occurred, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Ingestion time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the Vercy record captured the fact, stored separately from event and observation instants.

data_elements.name: Change significance code
data_elements.description: Code distinguishing editorial, corrective and substantive changes and driving the re-approval requirement.

artifacts.name: Decision lifecycle and change ledger
artifacts.description: An append-only, per-decision ledger of governance acts: status transitions, approvals bound, delegations exercised, versions issued, supersessions, holds placed and released, and disclosure decisions. Entries are never edited or removed; corrections are added as new entries that reference the entry they correct.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each ledger instance is named {decision-master-identifier}-GOVLED-{NNNN}, where the decision master identifier is the authoritative master-system identifier of the decision, GOVLED is the fixed artefact-kind discriminator, and NNNN is a zero-padded monotonic sequence scoped to that decision master record. Sequence values are never reused and never derived from any date, timestamp or period label; individual entries carry their own ordinal within the instance.

findings.name: Provenance of the governed decision content
findings.description: Records which agents generated, revised and attested the governed content in which qualified roles, from which prior drafts or decisions it was derived, how cited claim and evidence records are referenced without restatement, and whether the record was created natively or imported.

questions.text: Which agents generated, revised and attested the governed decision content, and in which qualified roles did they act?
answer_data: Attribution entries with agent reference and qualified role
Distinction between drafting, reviewing and attesting acts
Whether any generating agent was automated and, if so, its identifier

questions.text: From which prior decisions, drafts, submissions or precedents was this decision derived?
answer_data: Derivation references with relation type such as revision of, derived from or based on precedent
Ordering of derivation steps where a chain exists
Indicator of whether a derivation crosses an organisational boundary

questions.text: How are cited claim and evidence records referenced so that their content is not restated in this model?
answer_data: Claim and evidence references as identifiers with their owning model identifiers
Explicit prohibition on copying claim text, evidence appraisal or quality grades locally

questions.text: How is an imported or migrated decision distinguished from one created natively in this Dimension?
answer_data: Capture mode code covering native creation, import, migration and reconstruction
Source system reference and the ingestion instant
Confidence or completeness flag for reconstructed records

data_elements.name: Attribution entry
data_elements.description: An agent's qualified association with the generation, revision or attestation of the governed content.

data_elements.name: Derivation reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a prior decision, draft or precedent from which this decision was derived, with the relation type.

data_elements.name: Cited claim reference
data_elements.description: Identifier-only reference to a claim record owned by the parent knowledge-assertion model.

data_elements.name: Cited evidence reference
data_elements.description: Identifier-only reference to an evidence record; evidence appraisal, quality and custody semantics remain in the evidence model.

data_elements.name: Capture mode code
data_elements.description: Code distinguishing native creation, import, migration and reconstruction, with the source system reference.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Provenance here is a graph of typed references between agents, activities and prior records, and is most defensible when held as data that can be projected into an interoperable provenance vocabulary. The narrative products it points at — the statement of reasons, the reasoning trace and the evidence records — are artefacts already owned by the reasoning area and the evidence model, so no new document is warranted.

bundles.name: Access, integrity and defensible disposition
bundles.description: How the decision and its governance metadata are classified for access and disclosure, how their integrity is anchored and linked to external audit trails, and how they are retained, held and defensibly disposed of.
bundles.rationale: Records remain authoritative only if their integrity is demonstrable, their accessibility is controlled and their disposition is defensible. ISO 15489-1 makes integrity, usability and appraisal-driven disposition constitutive of an authoritative record; NARA organises requirements around maintenance, disposal and transfer; NIST separates access enforcement, audit and disposal into controls owned by the operating system; Regulation 1049/2001 and the GDPR supply the disclosure and erasure profiles.

layers.name: Access classification, disclosure and integrity assurance
layers.description: The classification and disclosure schedule for each part of the decision, the exemptions and partial-access rules that apply, and the fixity, sealing and audit-linkage facts that make the record's integrity demonstrable.

findings.name: Access classification, exemptions and disclosure schedule
findings.description: Sets the access class for the decision and, separately, for its rationale and governance metadata; records the exemption grounds relied on to withhold, whether partial access by redaction is possible, when an embargo lapses, what register-level metadata stays discoverable, and which personal data must be minimised before disclosure.

questions.text: What access classification applies, and does it differ between the decision outcome, the rationale and the governance metadata?
answer_data: Access class code per addressed part of the record
Reference to the classification scheme and the classifying authority
Instant from which each classification applies

questions.text: Which exemption grounds justify withholding, and can partial access be granted by releasing the parts not covered by them?
answer_data: Exemption ground codes with the provision reference relied on
Partial-access feasibility flag and the redaction profile reference
Whether an overriding public-interest test was applied and its outcome

questions.text: When does an embargo lapse so that the decision becomes proactively publishable?
answer_data: Embargo end instant as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z
Publication channel reference and the party obliged to publish
Behaviour when the embargo lapses while a hold or an appeal is pending

questions.text: Which register-level metadata remains discoverable even when the content itself is withheld?
answer_data: Enumerated discoverable metadata set such as identifier, subject, deciding authority and date
Rule preventing a reference from itself revealing exempt content
Handling rule for sensitive items whose very existence is restricted

questions.text: Which personal data in participant and interest records must be minimised or masked before disclosure?
answer_data: Fields flagged as personal data with their masking rule
Lawful basis reference for retaining them despite minimisation
Party accountable for applying the masking before release

data_elements.name: Access class code
data_elements.description: Coded access classification applied to an addressed part of the decision record, with the classifying authority reference.

data_elements.name: Exemption ground code
data_elements.description: Coded ground relied on to withhold, referencing the provision that supplies it.

data_elements.name: Redaction profile reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the profile describing which parts are removed for a partial release and by what rule.

data_elements.name: Embargo end time
data_elements.description: Instant at which an embargo lapses, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Discoverable metadata set
data_elements.description: The enumerated set of register-level fields that remain discoverable when content is withheld.

artifacts.name: Decision access and disclosure schedule
artifacts.description: A per-decision schedule stating the access class of each addressed part, the exemption grounds and provisions relied on, the redaction profile for partial release, embargo instants and the discoverable register metadata. It is a governance instruction, not an access-control implementation or a log of accesses granted.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Named {decision-master-identifier}-GOVACC-{NNNN}, where the decision master identifier is the authoritative master-system identifier of the decision, GOVACC is the fixed artefact-kind discriminator, and NNNN is a zero-padded monotonic sequence scoped to that decision master record and incremented on each reissue of the schedule. Sequence values are never reused and are never derived from dates, review cycles or period labels.

findings.name: Fixity, sealing and audit linkage
findings.description: Records the digest algorithm and value sealing each governed version, who computed it, which signature, seal or timestamp-token reference evidences non-repudiation of the approval, how a failed verification is reported without altering the sealed version, and which external system holds the audit trail.

questions.text: Which digest algorithm and value seal each governed version, and which agent computed them at which instant?
answer_data: Named digest algorithm and its digest value per version
Computing agent reference and computation instant
Canonical form over which the digest was computed

questions.text: Which signature, seal or timestamp-token reference evidences non-repudiation of the approval?
answer_data: Signature or seal reference with the signing agent and scheme identifier
Timestamp-token reference where third-party time attestation exists
Validation status of the signature at the last verification

questions.text: How is a failed integrity verification reported without altering the sealed version?
answer_data: Verification outcome entry with expected and observed digest values and the verification instant
Escalation target and notification obligation on failure
Rule that the sealed version is quarantined rather than corrected in place

questions.text: Which external audit or event-log system holds the trail for this record, and which identifier links the two?
answer_data: Audit system reference and the correlation identifier
Statement that audit-record generation, protection and retention are owned by that system
Coverage note stating which governance acts are expected to appear in the external trail

data_elements.name: Digest algorithm
data_elements.description: Named cryptographic digest algorithm used to seal a governed version.

data_elements.name: Digest value
data_elements.description: Digest computed over the declared canonical form of a governed version.

data_elements.name: Signature or seal reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the signature, seal or timestamp token evidencing non-repudiation of an approval.

data_elements.name: Verification outcome entry
data_elements.description: Result of an integrity verification with expected and observed values, outcome code and verification instant.

data_elements.name: Audit trail reference
data_elements.description: Correlation reference to the external system that generates and retains the audit trail for this record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Integrity facts are small, machine-checkable values attached to versions and must be verifiable independently of any document rendition; a document would itself need sealing and would create a recursion. Crucially, the audit trail that these values correlate to is generated, protected and retained by an external system, so this finding holds references only and does not materialise an audit artefact whose semantics this model does not own.

layers.name: Retention, legal hold and defensible disposition
layers.description: The retention schedule binding and its trigger, the legal hold state, the authorisation and evidence for disposition, the surviving tombstone facts and the archival transfer path for records of permanent value.

findings.name: Retention binding, legal hold and defensible disposition
findings.description: Binds the decision record to a retention schedule and its start trigger, records whether a legal hold is in force and by whom, states which facts survive when deletion is authorised and which model executes disposition, evidences destruction or transfer, and identifies records of permanent value destined for archival transfer rather than destruction.

questions.text: Which retention schedule and issuing authority govern this decision record, and which event starts the retention clock?
answer_data: Retention schedule reference with issuing authority and item number
Retention trigger code such as decision effective, superseded, closed or last accessed
Retention period expressed as a duration from the trigger instant

questions.text: Is a legal hold or disposition freeze in force, who imposed it, and when was it released?
answer_data: Hold entries with imposing authority reference, ground and scope
Imposition and release instants as RFC 3339 timestamps with explicit offset or Z
Rule suspending all disposition actions while any hold is in force

questions.text: When deletion is authorised, which facts survive in the tombstone and which model or Dimension policy executes the disposition?
answer_data: Surviving tombstone fields: decision master identifier, version identifier, deciding authority reference, status at disposition, disposition authorisation reference and disposition instant
Named executing owner: the carrying record model and the adopting Dimension's records authority
Statement of which erasure rule, if any, overrides the tombstone-first default

questions.text: How is destruction, transfer or migration evidenced so that the disposition remains defensible?
answer_data: Disposition evidence reference such as a certificate or receipt identifier
Authorising party reference and the authorisation instant
Ledger entry recording the disposition act with its separated time axes

questions.text: Which decisions are appraised as being of permanent value and transferred to an archival authority rather than destroyed?
answer_data: Appraisal outcome code and the appraising authority reference
Archival destination reference and transfer instant
Transfer format and metadata expectations stated by the receiving authority

data_elements.name: Retention schedule reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the retention schedule item and its issuing authority that governs this record.

data_elements.name: Retention trigger code
data_elements.description: Coded event that starts the retention period, with the instant at which the trigger occurred.

data_elements.name: Legal hold entry
data_elements.description: A hold on disposition with imposing authority reference, ground, scope, imposition instant and release instant.

data_elements.name: Disposition action code

data_elements.name: Tombstone record
data_elements.description: The minimal surviving set of identity, authority, status and disposition facts retained after an authorised deletion of content.

data_elements.name: Archival transfer destination reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the archival authority or repository receiving a record appraised as permanent.

artifacts.name: Decision review, hold and disposition record
artifacts.description: A per-decision record of appraisal outcome, retention binding, holds imposed and released, disposition authorisation and the evidence of destruction, transfer or migration. It states and evidences the disposition decision; it does not perform the disposition, which is executed by the carrying record model and the adopting Dimension's records authority.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Named {decision-master-identifier}-GOVDIS-{NNNN}, where the decision master identifier is the authoritative master-system identifier of the decision, GOVDIS is the fixed artefact-kind discriminator, and NNNN is a zero-padded monotonic sequence scoped to that decision master record and incremented for each disposition cycle. Sequence values are never reused and never derived from a date, retention year or schedule period.

functions.name: Frame the decision
functions.description: Establish the governed decision record: mint or bind its identifier, classify it against a decision type and jurisdictional profile, state the decision question and admissible answer space, record the triggering issue, objectives and critical success factors, and declare context dependencies and binding constraints.
inputs: Decision type code and jurisdictional profile identifier
Decision question text and admissible answer space
Objectives, critical success factors and impacted indicator references
Declared constraints, required input references and upstream decision references
outputs: Framed decision record carrying a resolvable identifier and version discriminator
Recorded decision question with its admissible answer space
Derived list of profile-required content elements
preconditions: An identifier is available from the identity priority order, master-system identifier first
The decision type and its bound profile are published by the profile custodian
effects: A uniquely identified decision record exists and is resolvable
Profile-required content elements are declared so later completeness checks are decidable
Framing content becomes the fixed reference against which the outcome statement is validated

functions.name: Register a candidate alternative
functions.description: Add a candidate alternative to the decision's alternative set with its own identifier, kind code and description, including registration of a no-action or business-as-usual baseline where the bound profile requires one.
inputs: Alternative kind code, including baseline or do-minimum where applicable
Variant-of reference where the alternative varies another
outputs: Registered alternative with its own identifier and registration ordinal
Updated alternative set for the decision
Baseline presence indicator for the bound profile
preconditions: The decision has been framed and its profile binding is known
The alternative is described in terms that the declared criteria can be applied to
effects: The alternative set is extended append-only; registered alternatives are never silently removed
Absence of a profile-required baseline becomes a detectable validation failure
Variants remain distinguishable from independently registered alternatives

functions.name: Declare the evaluation criteria and weights
functions.description: Record the criteria against which alternatives will be compared, each with its measure, scale, unit and preference direction, the separation of mandatory pass-or-fail criteria from compensatory ones, and the weighting scheme with its declared method or an explicit statement that no weighting is used.
inputs: Objectives and critical success factors from the framed decision
Candidate criteria with measures, scales and preference directions
Weighting method identifier and weight values where a weighting scheme applies
Monetisation convention where a criterion is expressed in monetary terms
outputs: Declared criterion set addressable by criterion identifier
Declared weighting scheme, or an explicit no-weighting statement
Classification of criteria as mandatory or compensatory
preconditions: Objectives and constraints have been framed
Each criterion is stated in terms that permit a result to be recorded against it
effects: Alternatives can be scored against a fixed and citable criterion set
Criteria that also act as eligibility filters are linked to the screening criteria
Weighting remains optional so that decisions without a weighting scheme are still complete

functions.name: Evaluate and compare the alternatives
functions.description: Record, as governed decision content, one evaluation round: eligibility screening results with reasons for exclusion, per-criterion results for admitted alternatives, any aggregation and ranking, sensitivity findings, and citations to evidence. Running an executable rule set or decision service to produce those results is outside this model.
inputs: Declared criterion set and screening criteria
Recorded results per alternative and criterion
Evidence item references supporting results or assumptions
outputs: Eligibility and exclusion results with a recorded reason for each exclusion
Alternative-by-criterion comparison matrix for the round
Result status markers for contested, provisional or bias-adjusted results
preconditions: At least one alternative is registered and the criterion set is declared
The evaluation round ordinal is available and has not been used
effects: A serially numbered, append-only evaluation round is recorded and never edited in place
Every excluded alternative carries an explicit recorded reason
Cited evidence is bound by identifier and role only; evidence appraisal, integrity and provenance stay with the evidence model
Execution traces of any external decision service are not captured here

functions.name: Record the selected decision outcome
functions.description: Record the selected alternative, the disposition, the explicit outcome statement answering the decision question, the declared effect onset and applicability, the factors expressly balanced, any explained divergence from the ranking, and the attached conditions, unresolved matters and stated consequences.
inputs: Selected alternative reference or declared variant description
Disposition code from the controlled list
Balanced factors and divergence explanation where the top-ranked alternative was not selected
Attached conditions, unresolved matters, accepted risks and reopening triggers
outputs: Outcome statement bound to the recorded decision question
Disposition code and selected alternative reference
Condition, reservation, consequence and raised-concern sets
preconditions: The alternative set contains the selected alternative or the alternative the selected variant derives from
Profile-required comparison and baseline content is present
The outcome statement falls within the recorded admissible answer space where one is declared
effects: The decision question has an explicit, immutable recorded answer; changing it requires a superseding decision that cites this one
Divergence from the evaluation ranking carries a recorded explanation where it occurs
Approval execution, publication, filing and enforcement of the outcome remain with the referenced activity, record and implementation models
Any monitoring or compliance work the conditions direct is executed and tracked by those models, not here

functions.name: Bind a reason to governed claims and evidence citations
functions.description: Attach claim references and evidence citation bindings to a reason or premise, recording citation type, locator and stance, and reporting any reference that does not resolve in its owning model.
inputs: evidence references with citation type, locator and stance
outputs: persisted binding set attached to the reason
resolution report listing resolved, superseded and dangling references
preconditions: The reason record exists and names the decision it explains by its master-system identifier
Citation types are drawn from a governed citation-typing vocabulary with a declared version
Referenced claim and evidence identifiers are resolvable in WM-KNW-007 and WM-KNW-008 respectively
effects: Creates or revises binding records only; never creates, alters, grades or retracts a referenced claim or evidence item
Records unresolvable references as declared gaps rather than substituting local content

functions.name: Assemble premises, inference and conclusion into an argument structure
functions.description: Record an argument as premises, a first-class inference element carrying a scheme reference, and a conclusion, together with asserted support and conflict relations and any critical-question responses.
inputs: argument element references with role codes
inference scheme reference and catalogue version
preconditions: Every premise and conclusion slot references a governed claim or is explicitly marked as a local restatement
The scheme reference resolves in a declared catalogue, or the argument is flagged as informally schemed
effects: Records asserted inference and conflict only; performs no validity, soundness or entailment evaluation and issues no acceptability verdict
Leaves premise support status as asserted, without inferring support from the presence of a binding

functions.name: Re-check declared assumptions and sensitivity statements
functions.description: Compare declared assumptions, dependencies and sensitivity statements against the current state of the inputs and references they name, and annotate each with a status so that stale reasoning is visible.
inputs: assumption and dependency records with validity windows and defeat conditions
sensitivity variable references and recorded ranges
current resolution state of the referenced inputs
outputs: list of stale, defeated-by-declaration or unresolvable references
preconditions: Each assumption declares either a validity window, a defeat condition or an explicit unbounded marker
The referenced inputs expose a resolvable identity and revision
effects: Annotates existing records with a status and the time of the check; never edits the asserted assumption text
Does not execute the underlying analysis, does not re-run any model, does not enforce an outcome and does not change any decision state
Escalation, review scheduling and any consequent decision action are left to the `governance` split and the adopting Dimension

functions.name: Record an objection, counter-evidence or dissenting position
functions.description: Capture an objection or counter-argument against a named reason or inference, with its attribution, any counter-evidence binding, and an appended disposition where one has been stated.
inputs: objecting party reference and stated capacity
outputs: dissenting or minority opinion artefact where a position is preserved separately
preconditions: The targeted reason, premise or inference exists
The objecting party is identified by reference to a record held outside this model
effects: Appends objection and disposition records; existing objections and dissent are never overwritten or removed
Applies argument-level defeated markings without altering the recorded outcome or any decision state
Adjudication authority, quorum and approval workflow remain with the `governance` split and are not exercised here

functions.name: Produce a bounded, audience-scoped explanation rendition
